You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The snapshot looks like a period when rates are falling sharply, long yields are very low relative to the past 3 years, and gold is strongly up. The policy rate z-score is +1.0 but fell 3.0 over 3 months, so the Fed has been cutting rapidly from a high level. Core CPI is above its 3-year average, and headline CPI is below it. Unemployment is low relative to its 3-year average yet has risen, and payrolls are weak.

The 10-year yield z-score of -2.5 is extreme. That would fit a period after yields had been high for years and then dropped hard. March 2020 is one candidate, but the VIX is only +1.0, not extreme. Equities are -0.5 over 1 month, and the 12-month change is -1.5, which is mild.

Another candidate is mid-2019. The 3-year window of 2016-2019 saw the fed funds rate rising, so +1.0 fits. The 10-year fell sharply from 3.2% to 1.5% by August 2019, and gold rallied then. Unemployment was at a low, so -1.0 fits, with a slight rise. Payrolls were slowing. Core CPI was above average. Industrial production was weak. The VIX was elevated in August 2019. The 3-month policy rate change of -3.0 seems too large for 2019, though, since only one cut had occurred by August. By October 2019 there had been three cuts, and the 10-year was around 1.7%. The 2y-10y spread z of -1.5 doesn't fit 2019 well, though.

A third candidate is late 2024 or early 2025. The 3-year window is 2022-2024, with the policy rate high. However, the 10-year yield would not be -2.5 then.

A further candidate is September 2025 or later. The window is late 2022 to 2025, and the 10-year at 4.0% would be roughly -1.5. The policy rate z is +1.0 and the 3-month change is -3.0, which is unlikely.

A final candidate is 2008, when the window is 2005-2008 and the policy rate is higher than average. The policy rate fell sharply from 5.25% to 2% by March 2008, and the 10-year fell. Gold is strong, and Treasuries are strong with a negative equity-bond correlation. Unemployment at 5% is low relative to the window average. Core CPI is above average, and headline is below. But the VIX would be higher, and the 12m equity return is only -1.5. Early 2008 fits well, with January or February 2008 plausible. Equity 3m +0.5 doesn't fit very well, though. The 2y yield change of -1.5 over 3 months is small for that period, while the 12m change is -2.5.

Late 2019 is another fit, with the equity 3m at +0.5 and the 12m at -1.5 (the 12m is odd, since equities were up in 2019). I'll go with early 2008, around January.
